title: Translation invariance of the normalized affine-space integration
statement:
Use the finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, for arbitrary $n\geq1$, and the field $k$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $d\geq0$, and put $V=\mathbf A^d_S$ with projection $q:V\to S$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Work in the ordinary etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of the schemes $T$ below [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with the ordinary etale Tate line and its pullback identifications [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Put $L=A_V(d)[2d]$ and let $t_q:Rq_!L\to A_S$ be the normalized trace [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], with ordinary compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

For a section $a:S\to\mathbf A^d_S$, let $\tau_a:V\to V$ be the $S$-automorphism $z\mapsto z-a$. For the Cartesian square with both vertical maps $q$, bottom map $1_S$ and top map $\tau_a$, let $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau_a}:Rq_!L\to Rq_!\tau_a^*L$ be the canonical compact-support exchange, normalized as in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and let $\kappa_a:\tau_a^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ be the Tate pullback identification. Then the actual derived morphisms satisfy
$$t_q\circ Rq_!(\kappa_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau_a}=t_q.$$
This equality includes the universal translation over $P=\mathbf A^d_S$, with $a$ its tautological section after base change, and commutes with every base change $S'\to S$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Under the specified Tate and compact-support comparisons [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], it is also the equality of the corresponding pro-etale integration maps. Concretely, at every annihilating prime-power level, use the trivial rank-d bundle integration `vectorIntegration` and its canonical `vectorSite` comparison; the affine-trace counit is identified with `vectorBundleIntegration` by the affine vector-integration construction [def-amb-vector-integration].

proof.text: Finite type over the specified field makes S Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Use the published coordinate-tower theorem [lem-trf-ambient-affine-translation-trace] for the actual translation exchange and Tate comparison. It states action followed by the normalized affine trace equals that trace. The normalized trace is invertible by [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], for the precise transport and projective-line datum selected by ambientAffineTraceTransport and ambientAffineTraceDatum. Cancel this trace to prove that affineTranslationAction is the identity, for every Noetherian base, every coordinate section and every rank, including zero.

Apply the identity of the ordinary action on the affine parameter scheme, with its inherited Noetherian structure and universal coordinates; composing with the trace gives the universal ordinary equation. For each annihilating prime-power level on any Noetherian base, unfold proEtaleAffineTranslationAction. Its middle factor is the comparison image of the identity. Functoriality and the hom-inverse identities for the specified chart bridge and vectorSite cancel the conjugation, giving the identity on the actual pro-etale integration source. Compose it with the actual vectorIntegration. This proves both the pointwise and universal pro-etale clauses without needing to identify the chart bridge composite with integration.

For every section a the ordinary trace equation follows by replacing the action by the identity. After any finite-type base change, use the same identity over S and S′ to prove the displayed action square by functoriality. The remaining displayed trace square is exactly the arbitrary-Noetherian-base-change clause of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] for the selected normalized transport and datum; unfold affineTranslationBaseChange and reassociate. Assemble these equations and the pro-etale clauses into AffineTranslationTraceCompatibility.

statement_change.what: The recorded theorem dependency was incorrectly being treated as a statement dependency even though the item uses only the module's plain coordinate definitions; the pro-etale sentence also needed the actual vectorIntegration/vectorSite maps and their affine vector-integration bridge.

old_proof.text: First work on the ordinary étale site. The finite-type $k$-scheme $S$ is Noetherian, and so are $P=\mathbf A^d_S$ and $V_P=V\times_SP$; the affine polynomial charts give the needed separated finite-type maps. Let $q_P:V_P\to P$ be the base change of $q$, let $a_P:P\to V$ be the tautological section, and let $\tau_P:V_P\to V_P$ be $(z,a)\mapsto(z-a,a)$. It is an automorphism over $P$, with inverse $(z,a)\mapsto(z+a,a)$. Apply [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] to $q_P$, $\tau_P$, and the canonical pullback isomorphism $\tau_P^*L\simeq L$. This gives the actual compact-support action $\rho_P:Rq_{P!}L\to Rq_{P!}L$ and its compatibility with every base change. By the base-change clause of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], the normalized trace $t_P:Rq_{P!}L\to A_P$ is an isomorphism and is the pullback of $t_q$ along $P\to S$.

old_proof.text: Conjugate the universal action by the specified trace: $\alpha=t_P\circ\rho_P\circ t_P^{-1}:A_P[0]\to A_P[0]$. It is an automorphism of the constant $A_P$-module sheaf. By full faithfulness of degree-zero sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], it is induced by a unique $A_P$-linear sheaf automorphism $\alpha_0$. Module linearity makes $\alpha_0$ multiplication by $b=\alpha_0(1)$, and the inverse action shows that $b$ is a unit. The section $b$ is a Zariski-locally constant function with values in $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant]. Pullback of $b$ along any base-change section is the scalar by which the corresponding translated trace is multiplied, by the action and trace base-change equations in the two cited lemmas.

old_proof.text: For every geometric point $\bar s\to S$, the fibre $P_{\bar s}=\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ is nonempty and connected: its coordinate ring is a nonzero domain (and for $d=0$ it is the one-point scheme). The restriction of $b$ to this fibre is locally constant, and its value at the origin is $1$, because the universal translation restricted along the zero section is the identity and [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] gives $\rho_{1,1}=1$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-connected-locally-constant-map] makes $b|_{P_{\bar s}}=1$. Every point of $P$ lies in such a geometric fibre, so the section/function identification of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] gives $b=1$ globally. Therefore $\alpha=1$ and $t_P\circ\rho_P=t_P$.

old_proof.text:
Pull the universal equality back along the section $a:S\to P$. The action base-change identity of [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] identifies the pulled-back action with $Rq_!(\kappa_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau_a}$, while the affine trace base-change identity of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] identifies the pulled-back $t_P$ with $t_q$. Thus
$$t_q\circ Rq_!(\kappa_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau_a}=t_q.$$
The same argument after any $S'\to S$ gives the asserted universal and arbitrary-base-change compatibility. Finally [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] carries this actual ordinary étale equality, with the specified Tate and compact-support comparisons, to the corresponding pro-étale integration maps.
